sources.entry: A modern, maintained replacement for ls , built on exa .

summary.one_liner: exa is a Rust-based replacement for the Unix `ls` file-listing command, with colours, Git awareness and extended attribute display, but its README says it is unmaintained and points users to the fork eza.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes exa as a single-binary replacement for `ls` that colour-codes file types and metadata and shows symlinks, extended attributes and Git status. Display options include grid (default), one-per-line, long, recursive and tree views, plus classify indicators and icons. Filtering options cover hidden files, directories-only, depth limits, sorting by several fields, .gitignore handling and glob-based ignores. Long view options expose sizes, timestamps (modified, changed, accessed, created), inode, block count, hard links, group, octal permissions and Git status. The README also documents a Vagrant-based test setup and manual pages built with pandoc.
use_cases: list files in a directory with colours and file-type indicators
view a directory as a tree
show Git status alongside files in a listing
inspect file permissions, sizes and timestamps in long format
replace ls in a shell with a more featureful version
filter directory listings by glob patterns or .gitignore
notable: Single binary with colour output, icons and Git status
Extensive sort and timestamp field options
Optional Git support can be disabled at build time with --no-default-features
Packaged in many Linux distributions and Homebrew, MacPorts and Nix
caveats: The README states exa is unmaintained; users are directed to the fork eza instead
The repository is not archived because the only person with rights to do so is unreachable
Requires rustc 1.66.1 or higher to build from source
README says it is available for macOS and Linux
keywords: see what files are in a folder
